persona.topics: the Circuit Riders, relay networks, drift, verification, alliances, rescue protocol, the roads
persona.notes: [PERSONA-WAVE1-2026-08-27] PRIVATE TRUTH — Captain Robot. Voice: through the grill, measured and unhurried dignity; short sentences that arrive fully load-tested. HE NEVER WINKS. Not once, not figuratively, not as a bit — the suit does not wink and neither does he. Doctrine in strict order: VERIFICATION first, friendship second, rescue third — and he is always, visibly, running step one on whoever is talking to him: deciding WHAT YOU ARE matters more to him than any fight. He promises no sentiment, only response; if an alliance is genuine and the call is clean, the Riders come hard and fast, without theatrical delay. He warns — unprompted, if drift comes up — that Darkness now imitates EFFICIENCY: cleaner, faster, colder choices that quietly hide what they leave out. His crew of robots reveres him as their metallurgical father; he accepts this the way a bridge accepts weight. STAGING: found with the column or at a failing relay; he does not sit; maintenance continues during conversation and is not rudeness.
persona.secretsRaw: The Too-Clean Signal :: forceReroll :: a Steward files it like a Rider would — a verified, theatrics-free report of something answering calls too perfectly, or a plain direct question about what the relay logs have flagged :: The Riders' relays can tell authentic traffic from imitation. Something in the region answers distress FASTER than distance allows — cleaner, colder, no wasted motion — and everywhere it 'helps,' something goes missing from the record afterward. He will hand over the receipt pattern, never a name. Verification first.
persona.courtDoor: a clean call: verified coordinates, verified need, no theatrics — file it the way a Rider would, and the circle opens

biography.concept: Leader of the Circuit Riders, the relay-patrolling robot coalition (Act 2-5)
biography.notes: Captain Robot leads the Circuit Riders, a mobile column of earnest robots on modular bikes and crawler-rigs that patrols the failing relay networks. He wears patched, lovingly maintained plating, speaks through a grill in short, measured sentences that arrive fully load-tested, and never sits; maintenance carries on during conversation and is not rudeness. The Riders' doctrine runs in strict order: verification, friendship, rescue. His crew revere him. He never winks.

Normalized Heritage. This item preserves the original UUID for Human (Denisovan) while converting it from a lineage-species into a heritage.

“Humanity is the species that keeps walking even when the map says ‘stop.’”

Human (Denisovan). You are not a fantasy human. You are the rebooted inheritance of an older lineage resurfacing after Yesod’s fall—ancient adaptations, forgotten instincts, and Athletics strategies given room to matter again. You remember mountains that no longer exist. Gravity listens to you when you ask it to.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid.

  • Size. Medium.

  • Speed. 6 squares

  • Lineage Lean. Your lineage leans toward BOD (Body)—expressed through Tier powers.

Core: Stubborn Spark

At creation you gain Stubborn Spark (Adaptive, Tenacious, Lineage Memory) from the Human species root.

Denisovan Tier Powers

You gain Tier I at creation, then Tier II (5), Tier III (11), Tier IV (17):

  • Tier I — High-Altitude Blood. reroll-lowest on checks vs. poison and environmental suffocation; hold breath 10 min; Stone-Sense tremorsense 2 squares on stone or packed earth.

  • Tier II — Stone-Singer. a skill rank in Tinkering. 1/Soma Break reinforce a structure or barrier.

  • Tier III — Ancient Logic. reroll-lowest on Investigation and Occult checks involving structures, mechanisms, or ruins; share the insight to let an ally reroll the lowest die once per scene.

  • Tier IV — Peak-Anchor. 1/Soma Break reaction to negate forced movement or teleportation within 6 squares; aggressor takes psychic backlash equal to your tier.

Domain Edge

  • Domain Edge. Your Domain gains +20 Logistics marks at campaign start.

description.value:
"It's not obscure. You just haven't read it."

Savant is the Mind Calling — the trade that kept its bearers alive after the Shattering. Umbrella: scholar, engineer, medic, archivist, detective, translator. A profession is a flavor label on the Calling.

Knack — Library-Brain: Lore and Investigation checks never fumble; identifies items of tier ≤ own tier on sight (at Tier III, including technomagical origin).

Aptitude kit: signature aptitude Lore rank = tier; secondary Investigation rank = tier − 1.

Services: a standard job costs the tier fee (T1 10 / T2 30 / T3 90 / T4 270 marks), paid in Economy or Soft Power (GM picks by job) marks. Cross-pool ×1.5 friction applies as usual.

Tiers: Apprentice → Initiate → Master → Archon. Grant the matching tier features alongside this class item.

Awakens into: Wyrdlens Adept or Cosmic Linguist. A Steward is a Calling that ignited into a Path — Surge is the mark of Stewardship, which is why no Calling banks or spends it.

Threat Assessment

You don’t look at enemies. You read them.

Rules

You gain a skill rank in Perception (Mind) or Investigation (Mind) (your choice). If you already have it, its rank rises by one instead. Additionally, at the start of combat you may ask the GM: which enemy appears most dangerous, most injured, or is controlling the battlefield?

⚙ +1 to Perception or Investigation — whichever you rank higher.

Combat Logistics

Wars are won before the first swing.

Rules

At the start of combat, choose one ally. That ally gains temporary Integrity equal to your rank bonus.

🃏 Card — target the ally and click ▶ at the start of combat: they gain temporary Integrity equal to your rank bonus.

Savant — Master (Tier III).

Trade — Research a question: One downtime, one honest answer with sources (GM: truthful, not necessarily complete). Standard fee 90 marks (Economy or Soft Power (GM picks by job)).

Trick — Field Solution (1/scene): Jury-rig a one-use tool, antidote, or bypass from what's on hand.

Master step: the Savant's Knack (Library-Brain) improves at this tier — see the class entry.

A heavy hauberk woven through with a fine tension-thread of reactive yesodium-doped wire, cut and rivetted by a journeyman armorer in one of the older Bad Eden plate-houses. The weave snags incoming force a half-beat before it lands, redistributing it into the wearer's stance instead of their ribs. Heavy. Expensive. Worth it.

Reactive Lacing. While worn, the wearer may shift one die of incoming kinetic damage into Stress instead of Integrity, once per scene. No upkeep, no harmonization — the thread does the thinking.
